reasons: Scope is correct: Section 4.9(a) is an inspection/verification right binding us (Ono, the licensee) that lets Array itself enter our facilities and examine internal procedures and records to verify compliance 'with this Agreement' with no frequency cap, only 'reasonable advance notice' and no cost allocation - unlimited/unfixed audits are walk-away territory under AUDIT, so 'deviation' is the right classification and not over-flagging.

No double-flagging: the finding correctly treats the Section 7.4 royalty audit (once per Calendar Year, independent nationally recognised auditor acceptable to us, confidentiality undertaking, Array's expense subject to an underpayment threshold) as sitting at or above the fallback and leaves it un-redlined, noting the un-quantified notice and redacted percentage only in the rationale, which matches the playbook's classification semantics.

Redline is actionable, grammatical and additive: it inserts a once-per-twelve-months cap, thirty (30) days' prior written notice and Array's cost into the existing notice phrase while preserving the substantive inspection language, i.e. the smallest edit that reaches the playbook position; the failed 'minimal edit' check (ratio 0.602) is advisory and not borne out by the rendered text, which is an insertion of roughly 25 words into a long paragraph.

Comment is accurate, correctly scoped to 4.9(a), cites the playbook limits, mirrors the already-agreed Section 7.4 mechanics and offers the 15-day fallback, in the required concise first-person-plural tone with the [Playbook] prefix.

Minor and properly non-fatal: the edit does not add the preferred 'independent auditor bound by confidentiality' requirement and states Array's cost unconditionally rather than with an underpayment shift; the former is a preferred-only sub-element and the latter is favourable to us and appropriate for a non-payment inspection.
